description:
Finding: RuntimeEnvironment (stoa_core/src/env.rs) classifies the process as Production/Development/Test based on STOA_ENV. The startup banners in all five daemons emit this classification. But the security guards that abort on dangerous configs (dev-mode auth on non-loopback) do NOT consult RuntimeEnvironment — they check config.auth.is_dev_mode() && !is_loopback_addr(). So it is possible to run with STOA_ENV=production but have auth dev-mode active on a loopback address (legitimate dev/test), or conversely to run STOA_ENV=development but still have full auth configured (no guard fires, which is fine). The two systems are orthogonal and that is probably correct, but nowhere is it written down.

Risk: A future maintainer sees RuntimeEnvironment::is_dev() and assumes 'if I set STOA_ENV=development I am in dev mode and the guards will behave differently'. They would be wrong — the guards are purely config-based. This leads to confusion when trying to understand why a STOA_ENV=development daemon still refuses to start (because the auth guard fires on the listen address, not the env var). Conversely they might expect that STOA_ENV=production would tighten guards, and be surprised it does not.

Suggested fix: Add a comment in env.rs near RuntimeEnvironment explaining that RuntimeEnvironment controls logging/banner only; startup security guards (auth dev-mode, signing key, admin token) are config-structure-based and do not consult this enum. This is a two-line comment, not a code change.
title: No documentation of gap between RuntimeEnvironment and address-based guards
